subject: System Design
title: Autocomplete at Scale
description: A quick, practical guide to Autocomplete at Scale.

hook.text: You type 'how to' and instantly see 10 suggestions. Google processes your keystrokes faster than you can type them.

buildup.text: Autocomplete uses a trie data structure that stores all common queries as a tree of characters for fast prefix lookups.

discovery.text: Suggestions are ranked by popularity, recency, and personalization. The most-searched completions appear first.

twist.text: Autocomplete must respond in under 100ms or it feels laggy. The data is pre-computed and served from edge caches.

climax.text: Autocomplete is a search engine within the search engine — optimized for speed above all else.

punchline.text: Pre-computed trie, served from the edge — under 100ms.

quiz.question: Why is autocomplete data pre-computed?
options: To respond in under 100ms as the user types
